issues.failure_explanation: Eliminated face DoFs are reconstructed from the volume projector Pi_m^K, not from shared face data. Consequently, equal preserved boundary DoFs need not give equal traces. For example, on a centered cube take an edge space with m=1, preserved beta_d=mu_r=1 and k_d=0, and original beta_d'=2. The retained DoFs already compute Pi_1 by propcompoly. Set all preserved boundary data to zero and choose the retained volume data so Pi_1 v=(x,y,0). On a horizontal face, the eliminated moment against x_F x^2 then equals the positive integral of (x^2+y^2)x^2. The tangential trace is therefore nonzero, although every shared retained boundary DoF agrees with an adjacent zero function. This defect persists even when the L2 projector is genuinely computable.

failure_location.quote: Since boundary continuity, operator conformity and B-compatibility\cite{boffiMixedFiniteElement2013} (Remark 5.1.6) are preserved, the method is applicable to a wide range of PDEs and numerical techniques, just as the original VEM.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, eliminated boundary data must be reconstructed trace-locally and consistently between neighboring cells, and the resulting volume spaces and interpolation estimates must be re-established.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted global H(curl) conformity is not ensured by the proposed DoF assembly; the analogous reduction of nodal face moments also fails to ensure H1 conformity.
issues.title: Cellwise projection constraints do not preserve conformity across faces
issues.why_classification: Restoring the advertised conformity requires a compatible boundary-space construction, not merely a local estimate or additional smoothness assumption.

issues.failure_explanation: Injectivity of the retained DoFs on S does not determine the moments (v,p) for arbitrary v in V. On the unit cube, take V=span{1,x}, S=span{1}, F_1(v)=v(0,0,0), and F_2(v)=integral_K v. These are unisolvent DoFs and F_1 identifies S, but F_1(x)=0 while Pi_S x=1/2. Moreover, the sole reduced constraint F_2(v)=F_2(Pi_S v) is automatic, so the proposed V^S remains two-dimensional although only one DoF is retained. Thus both computability and unisolvence of the reduced space fail. The later replacement of Pi_m I^S v by Pi_m I v relies on the same false implication.

issues.failure_explanation: The source allows m=0, when the face space has k_d=-1 and hence zero divergence. Its preserved constant normal moments must therefore have zero total flux. For the smooth field v=(x,y,z) on the unit cube, however, those prescribed moments have total flux 3. No interpolant in the stated space can match them. This field also satisfies the face theorem's m=0 regularity conditions with s=1 and r=0. Likewise, beta_r=m-1=-1 in the lowest-order edge construction is incompatible with interpolating arbitrary nonzero face circulations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce a lowest-order exception using constant divergence and face-curl polynomial spaces instead of degree -1, with the corresponding commuting projections. Alternatively, explicitly restrict degree -1 interpolants to compatible inputs, which would narrow the advertised scope.
issues.overall_effect: The commuting proposition is not valid for arbitrary smooth lowest-order inputs, and the unrestricted lowest-order face interpolation theorem refers to a nonexistent interpolant.
issues.title: Lowest-order derivative constraints make unrestricted interpolation impossible
issues.why_classification: A standard local lowest-order exception preserves general-order approximation and conformity goals without changing the higher-order construction.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof checks boundary curl moments and zero divergence, but not the reduced interior constraints needed for membership in the serendipity face space. For a removed test q=x_K cross p, an edge field w satisfies (curl w,q)=(curl Pi_m w,q). Membership of curl w in the corresponding face serendipity space instead requires (curl w,q)=(Pi_{m-1} curl w,q). These are different conditions: L2 projection does not generally commute with curl. The analogous mismatch occurs between nodal and edge reductions under the gradient. Thus the integration-by-parts identities for the original spaces do not establish either closure under differentiation or the asserted serendipity interpolation identities.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, construct compatible reduced spaces and projectors for which differentiation preserves every reduced constraint, and prove equality of all target DoFs rather than only boundary moments.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed serendipity exact sequence, curl interpolation estimate, gradient interpolation argument, and operator-based applications lack the required commuting-space construction.
issues.title: The L2-serendipity reductions are not shown to form a commuting complex
issues.why_classification: A commuting complex is a central guarantee, and obtaining it requires a new compatibility construction or abandoning that guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: Even interpreting the obvious curl/gradient slip in [3] as the gradient identity used in its proof, the identity fails without degree compatibility. The integration-by-parts boundary term requires edge moments through degree k_f, whereas nodal interpolation preserves only degrees through k-2. No condition k_f<=k-2 is imposed. This already fails with no serendipity reduction: on the unit cube take k=2, k_f=k_v=1 and v=x^3. Its edge interpolant is 3x^2/2-x/2. On a horizontal face, testing the gradient moment with x_F(x-1/2) gives a boundary-moment discrepancy of 1/120, although the nodal face moments agree.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the boundary-moment compatibility condition k_f<=k-2, retain k_v<=k_f, and state the matching node/edge parameter choices explicitly.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed gradient commuting identity is false for allowed degree choices independently of the L2-serendipity compatibility problem.
issues.title: Gradient commutation needs an unstated boundary-moment degree condition
issues.why_classification: The intended polynomial orders remain available after a short local degree restriction, and the displayed integration-by-parts argument then handles this particular obstruction.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition permits an original space with beta'>m or beta_r'>m-1 and preserves only the stated lower-order DoFs. Such a choice reduces some DoFs of types [1] and [3]. The proof nevertheless treats the original and serendipity interpolants as having identical complete edge traces and face-curl data, and omits their differences from the stability estimate. This omission survives making the L2 projector computable and repairing the commuting-complex issue.

issues.failure_explanation: From v in H^s one obtains grad v in H^{s-1}, not H^s, so the displayed right-hand seminorm is not defined under the hypotheses and the edge theorem cannot be applied at the claimed regularity. The endpoint is false even for smooth functions: choose m=1, s=2, an allowed original nodal space with linear edge traces, and v=x^2. Then |grad v|_2=0, so the estimate would force exact gradient interpolation, which is impossible with linear edge traces. More generally, degree-(m+1) polynomials contradict the stated s=m+1 endpoint.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the estimate by the standard-order bound ||grad(v-Iv)|| <= C h^{s-1}|v|_s, and justify it using an edge estimate of degree m-1 applied at regularity s-1, including the curl-free lowest-order endpoint.

As \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_{l}\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\) monotonically increases with \(l\), it must converges as \(l\rightarrow\infty\).

issues.failure_explanation: A fixed-degree stability estimate does not supply the asserted bound independent of l; the bound actually fails for a valid face family. On a centered cube take m=1, preserve k_r=0, and use original k_r'=l-1. The 21 retained DoFs determine Pi_1, whose polynomial range has dimension 12. Choose nonzero fixed retained data in its kernel. The corresponding fields w_l have fixed divergence and normal trace and are orthogonal to x_K cross P_{l-1}. A bounded L2 subsequence would have a weak limit w parallel to x_K with constant divergence. L2 regularity at the center forces w=c x_K, and Pi_1 w=0 then forces w=0, contradicting the fixed nonzero normal data. Hence the Lagrange bases cannot all satisfy the claimed l-independent bound.

failure_location.quote: \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_{l}\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\le \left\|\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\le C_{K}\) for some polytope dependent constant \(C_{K}\).

issues.failure_explanation: Even granting moment-column invariance and boundedness, convergence of projection norms does not establish an independent limiting family of functions. Polynomial density concerns a fixed function, whereas psi_i^l changes with l. Bounded independent families can lose rank in the limit: with P_{l+1} an orthogonal polynomial normalized at an endpoint, the functions 1-P_{l+1} and P_{l+1} are Lagrange functions for fixed mean/endpoint DoFs, but their projections through degree l have rank one for every l. Boundary and edge DoFs are not L2-continuous, so their normalization cannot simply be passed to an L2 limit. The proof supplies no additional argument using the face/edge structure to prevent this loss.

issues.failure_explanation: Only moments above the retained k_r are reduced. Retained type-[3] tests of degree greater than m need not vanish on ker Pi_m. The definition permits, for example, m=1 and k_r=k_r'=1, with no reduction. Choose a field with zero normal trace, zero divergence, zero linear cross-product moments, and a nonzero quadratic cross-product moment. Then Pi_1 v=0 but Pi_2 v is nonzero. Moreover Pi_2 v is orthogonal to all gradients in P_2, so it cannot lie in the asserted gradient subspace. The blanket annihilation claim therefore fails for allowed retained orders.

issues.failure_explanation: Even when every required cross-product moment does vanish, this implies L2 orthogonality to x_K cross P_{l-1}, not membership in the complementary gradient space. The displayed direct sum is not an L2-orthogonal decomposition. For instance, on a centered rectangular box with unequal side lengths, grad(xy)=(y,x,0) has nonzero inner product with x cross e_z=(y,-x,0). Thus the claimed image inclusion does not follow from the vanishing moments. The analogous curl/radial decomposition has the same distinction.

Its dimension can be computed by ordinary finite-dimensional linear algebra; under the stated annihilation conditions the same dimension difference is available.
